findings.issue: Shutdown abandons its live event-loop thread and pending tasks when startup cancellation cleanup stalls. The close timeout bounds only the calling thread, and subsequent close calls cannot finish teardown.
findings.evidence: Independent reviewer_lifecycle.py uses an offline fake whose start awaits forever and whose cancellation finally block awaits a controllable cleanup event. fetch_html(timeout_s=0.025) times out promptly. With cleanup still pending, close() raises TimeoutError after 35.009 seconds, while bridge._thread.is_alive() remains true and asyncio.all_tasks(bridge._loop) contains two tasks. A second close() returns in 0.000 seconds without stopping either task because _closed is already true. The loop stops only after the reviewer explicitly releases the fake cleanup event; no probe threads remain afterward. This is not a fake that suppresses cancellation indefinitely: its cleanup uses ordinary cancellable async waits, but shutdown never cancels/drains it after its grace period. shutdown() awaits the previous completion without a timeout, and loop.stop() is called only when shutdown finishes. Installed Crawl4AI BrowserManager.start() awaits rollback close()/playwright.stop(); BrowserManager.close() awaits browser.close()/playwright.stop() without an overall deadline. Playwright Connection.stop_async() awaits transport.wait_until_stopped(), backed by driver IO/process completion. A stalled driver therefore provides a realistic production trigger. An associated concurrent probe after _closed became true received TimeoutError after 0.065 seconds instead of an immediate closed RuntimeError because close holds the lock throughout its wait.
findings.fix: Give teardown an overall bounded lifecycle, including pending-operation rollback and crawler shutdown. After a bounded cleanup grace period, cancel and drain the outstanding tasks and ensure the loop/thread terminate, including on timeout/error; also bound the final task drain in _serve. Preserve serialization during ordinary rollback. Keep repeated close calls attached to unfinished teardown rather than treating a merely requested close as completed, and reject fetches immediately once closing begins. Add offline regressions for stalled cancellation cleanup and stalled crawler.close, asserting no live loop thread or pending tasks after close returns/raises and after a second close.
